## Install

**macOS / Linux**
```bash
curl -LsSf https://n-dimitrov.github.io/jtr/install.sh | sh
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**
```powershell
irm https://n-dimitrov.github.io/jtr/install.ps1 | iex
```

The installer fetches `uv` if needed, then installs this release. The same steps are on the [landing page](https://n-dimitrov.github.io/jtr/). No access to GitHub from your shell? Download the **Source code (zip)** below, extract it, and run the bundled `install.sh` / `install.ps1` — see [INSTALL.md](https://github.com/n-dimitrov/jtr/blob/main/INSTALL.md).

## What's new

**One-line install.** `install.sh` and `install.ps1` now download the latest release themselves when they aren't sitting next to an extracted release. Set `JTR_VERSION` to install a specific release. Running them from an extracted zip works as before.

**`jtr update`.** Installs the latest release and refreshes the `/jtr` Claude Code skill. `jtr update --check` only reports whether a newer release exists. On Windows a running program can't replace itself, so `jtr update` prints the installer one-liner to run instead; re-running the installer is the upgrade on every OS.

**The `/jtr` skill no longer goes stale.** Until now `jtr init` copied the skill into a project once and never touched it again, so upgrading jtr left the old skill text in place. Now:

- `jtr skill install` installs it for the current project, `jtr skill install --global` for every project (`~/.claude/skills/jtr`).
- `jtr skill update` refreshes the copies that exist, and `jtr update`, the installer and `jtr init` do the same.
- `jtr skill status` shows where the skill is installed and whether each copy is `current`, `outdated` or `modified`.

A copy you have edited is reported as `modified` and is never overwritten unless you pass `--force`. Copies installed by earlier releases are recognised and refreshed.

**Landing page.** <https://n-dimitrov.github.io/jtr/> has the install, setup, skill and update steps in one place.

## Behaviour changes

- `jtr init` now refreshes an outdated, unedited project skill instead of skipping it; `skills_installed` in its `--json` output lists the skill in that case too.
- Skill installs write a small `.jtr-skill.json` manifest next to `SKILL.md`.

## Upgrading

This is the last upgrade that needs the installer: run the one-liner above (or the zip flow). From 1.2.0 on, `jtr update` does it. No config, cookie, or `.env` change is required.
